chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, by a chain of his, that he was asked about a man who dies and leaves dependents and upon him is a debt, 'Should he spend upon them from his wealth?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is convinced that the debt which is upon him encompasses the entirety of the wealth, so he should not spend upon them, and if he is not convinced, so let him spend over them from the middle of the wealth.'
ai.seo_question: How should a deceased person's debt and family maintenance be balanced if the estate is insufficient to cover both fully?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of balancing creditor rights with family maintenance (nafaqah), prioritizing debt repayment only when it is certain to exhaust the estate. The instruction to spend from the 'middle' (wasat) of the wealth reflects a pragmatic approach to ensure equitable distribution without fully depleting assets before settling obligations. This nuance distinguishes between absolute certainty of insolvency and mere probability, a key distinction in Usuli fiqh.
